stories.title: Modi urges India Inc to suggest further reforms
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi asked industry leaders at the FICCI annual convention to suggest reforms for growth without hesitation. He also urged corporates to focus on self-reliance and heavy investment in agriculture. The government claims the pace of poverty reduction in India is currently very fast.

stories.title: Modi calls for India-centric global products
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged Indian firms to build quality products that carry India's identity to global markets. Addressing the FICCI annual convention, he called for an India First approach to guide investment decisions over the next 20 years. The industry is now tasked with serving global needs.

stories.title: CEA Nageswaran expects growth boost in FY28
stories.summary: Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran expects stronger growth and improved capital flows in FY28. He cited the easing of headwinds including energy market conditions and AI valuations. The government is currently preparing for the upcoming Union Budget with a more optimistic outlook than six months ago.

stories.title: Public sector banks report record profit
stories.summary: Public sector banks recorded a net profit of approximately 1.1 lakh crore rupees in the first half of FY27, a 17 percent increase. The Finance Ministry noted that improved return on assets may benefit the government and shareholders through higher dividends. There are currently 12 such banks.

stories.title: India-US trade deal faces delay
stories.summary: Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal stated that a bilateral trade deal cannot be signed until Washington establishes a new tariff architecture. The delay follows the US Supreme Court dismantling previous tariff frameworks. India is also awaiting the outcome of ongoing Section 301 investigations before proceeding with any agreement.

stories.title: CEA warns of rupee strength challenges
stories.summary: Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran said lower crude oil prices could provide a windfall for India in FY28. He added that robust capital inflows may create a new challenge in managing a strengthening rupee. The government is preparing for potential currency management issues next financial year.

stories.title: Government seeks permits for raw sugar imports
stories.summary: The government has invited importers to apply for zero-duty permits for 2.15 lakh tonnes of raw sugar by November 27. The move aims to address a domestic production shortfall expected for the current season. Previous permits for 8.12 lakh tonnes were already issued under the existing quota.

stories.title: Fresh bids opened for duty-free sugar imports
stories.summary: India has invited fresh applications from millers and refiners for the duty-free import of 215,044 tonnes of raw sugar. The bidding window remains open until November 27, 2026. The government order follows efforts to manage domestic sugar availability through the current calendar year.

stories.title: Mutual fund industry targets higher AUM-to-GDP ratio
stories.summary: The Association of Mutual Funds in India aims to grow assets under management, which currently sit at 22 percent of GDP. Despite market volatility, the industry reports 6.32 million unique investors. Mutual funds currently account for about 35 to 36 percent of total household financial savings.

stories.title: SpiceJet board approves 5,500 crore rupee raise
stories.summary: SpiceJet's board has approved a plan to raise up to 5,500 crore rupees to support the airline's revival and rebuild capacity. The board also authorized an increase in the company's share capital to 7,500 crore rupees. Management has been directed to close the investment discussions expeditiously.

stories.title: Auto stocks lead market rally
stories.summary: The Nifty 50 rose to 25,358 and the Sensex climbed 440 points on November 19, led by a rally in auto stocks. Maruti Suzuki shares surged 6.5 percent, while Tata Motors and Eicher Motors also saw gains. The broader market recovered from early session losses.

stories.title: Markets recover from early losses
stories.summary: Benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty recovered from early declines to trade in positive territory on Thursday. The rally was supported by foreign fund inflows and easing crude oil prices. This recovery occurred despite a hawkish tone in the latest US Federal Reserve policy meeting minutes.

stories.title: Auto stocks surge as input costs ease
stories.summary: The Nifty Auto index jumped nearly 4 percent as falling industrial metal prices eased concerns over manufacturing costs. Maruti Suzuki led the rally with a 7 percent gain, while Hyundai and Mahindra & Mahindra also advanced. Copper and aluminum prices recently hit multi-month lows.

stories.title: IT stocks decline for third session
stories.summary: The Nifty IT index fell for the third consecutive day, remaining 6.5 percent lower for November. Investors are booking gains following last month's rally amid concerns that US Federal Reserve rate hikes could weaken discretionary demand. Nine of the ten index constituents traded lower on Thursday.

stories.title: Indices slip on Fed rate hike signals
stories.summary: Benchmark indices fell on Thursday following hawkish signals from the US Federal Reserve minutes and a stronger dollar. The Nifty 50 opened lower at 25,186, while IT stocks led the broader market decline. Wednesday's session had already seen the Nifty shed 0.63 percent.

stories.title: Defence stocks rise on procurement plans
stories.summary: Shares of HAL, BEL, and BDL rose up to 3 percent on Thursday following government plans for a 20 percent increase in defence capital expenditure. The potential procurement pipeline includes 114 fighter jets and six submarines. Domestic manufacturers are expected to benefit from the proposed spending.

stories.title: Sensex falls 206 points to 81,837 in early trade, Nifty drops 78 points to 25,145 - Telegraph India
Markets open lower on Fed minutes
stories.summary: Indian equity benchmarks opened lower on Thursday as hawkish US Federal Reserve signals outweighed foreign buying. IT stocks led the decline due to fears that higher US rates will reduce client spending. The Sensex fell 0.25 percent to 81,830 in early trade.

stories.title: Indian shares set to open lower as Fed minutes signal hawkish stance
stories.summary: Indian shares are expected to open lower as US Federal Reserve meeting minutes suggest a need to intensify efforts to control inflation. While some policymakers considered further rate increases, the benchmark Nifty 50 index faces a negative start. Optimism over crude oil prices remains, for now.

stories.title: IndusInd Bank share price update
stories.summary: IndusInd Bank shares are trading at 915.55 with a price-to-earnings ratio of 23.7. The bank, which reports earnings per share of 38.52, currently holds a market capitalization of 71326.8. The liveblog continues to incorporate fundamental and technical indicators for those interested in the performance of the stock.

stories.title: Mahanadi Coalfields IPO opens for subscription
stories.summary: Mahanadi Coalfields Limited has opened its initial public offering to raise approximately 8,981.12 crore. The company set a price band of 129 to 136 per share, with a minimum investment of 14,960. The issue remains open until November 23, while the grey market reports a 3 premium.

stories.title: Mahanadi Coalfields raises 2,295 crore from anchor investors
stories.summary: Mahanadi Coalfields raised 2,295 crore from 53 anchor investors ahead of its IPO. Life Insurance Corporation of India and Nippon Life India Trustee were among the participants allotted shares at 136 apiece. The company's public subscription period begins on Thursday.

stories.title: Fairfax exits IIFL Finance in 3,454 crore stake sale
stories.summary: Fairfax Financial Holdings divested its 13.25 percent stake in IIFL Finance through a block deal involving 5.66 crore shares at 617 each. Major buyers included SBI Mutual Fund and HDFC Mutual Fund. The transaction follows board approval for a separate 5,000 crore investment proposal from Blackstone.

stories.title: KKR takes minority stake in Petronas renewable unit
stories.summary: KKR has acquired a minority stake in Gentari Renewables India, a subsidiary of Petronas. The investment aims to support the expansion of the company's renewable energy operations amid rising demand. Transaction details were not disclosed, though the company described KKR as a partner with a long-term approach.

stories.title: VedaCorp closes 1,600 crore A2B deal
stories.summary: Bodhi Tree Systems has acquired a majority stake in Adyar Ananda Bhavan for approximately 1,600 crore. The deal values the 60-year-old food brand at up to 3,400 crore. VedaCorp served as the dealmaker for the transaction, which aims to support the expansion of the company's outlets and overseas business.

stories.title: Piramal Pharma to acquire remaining Yapan Bio stake
stories.summary: Piramal Pharma will acquire the remaining 26 percent stake in its subsidiary Yapan Bio. The company's administrative committee has approved the exercise of a call option to buy the balance equity. Final terms, including the acquisition consideration and the effective date of the transfer, remain to be finalized.

stories.title: Style Union parent Nexon raises 485 crore
stories.summary: Nexon Omniverse, the parent firm of Style Union, raised 485 crore from Venturi Partners and Elev8 Venture Partners. The deal values the fashion retail chain at approximately 8,000 crore. The company plans to use the capital to expand its store network from the south into north and west India.

stories.title: Apple Maps updates navigation features in India
stories.summary: Apple has updated its Maps experience in India, adding 3D landmarks, lane guidance, and multi-stop routing. The update includes Natural Language Guidance, which provides conversational directions using real-world landmarks. The tech giant claims these features are intended to make travel and navigation easier for users across the country.

stories.title: SBI Funds and Punjab National Bank form distribution partnership
stories.summary: SBI Funds Management has partnered with Punjab National Bank to distribute its schemes through the bank's branch network. The partnership includes training for bank teams and digital support for customer onboarding. The fund house intends to leverage its experience with public sector banks to expand mutual fund participation.

stories.title: Fitch Ratings expects Blackstone investment to shift IIFL Finance strategy
stories.summary: Fitch Ratings suggests that Blackstone's planned 16 percent stake acquisition will make it the primary private-equity shareholder in IIFL Finance. The agency noted that the refreshed board composition could alter the firm's risk appetite and business model. Blackstone's capital infusion is intended to support the company's growth.

stories.title: Noida builder ordered to hand over flat after document failure
stories.summary: A consumer forum ordered JSS Buildcon to hand over a flat to a couple who paid 7.5 lakh toward a 77.35 lakh property. The commission ruled that the builder's failure to provide essential home loan documents constituted a deficiency in service. The handover must occur within 30 days.

stories.title: Consumer commission rules UPI PIN does not prove transaction consent
stories.summary: The Telangana State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission ordered SBI to refund 55,000 to a customer, plus 30,000 in costs. The commission observed that a UPI PIN does not by itself establish that an account holder authorized a disputed transaction. The bank has been held accountable for the loss.

stories.title: Survey finds 64 percent of Indian employees work unpaid hours
stories.summary: A survey of 36 markets by ADP Research found that 64 percent of Indian workers report working at least six unpaid hours per week. Senior leaders reported the heaviest workloads, with 34 percent of C-suite executives putting in extra time. Higher unpaid hours correlated with lower perceived productivity.

stories.title: Retail lending grows as defaults rise
stories.summary: India's retail lending book grew 18.8 percent to 185.2 lakh crore in the second quarter, according to CRIF. While consumer durable and personal loans drive new accounts, defaults in these segments are also increasing. Borrowers are encouraged to manage their debt carefully to avoid potential financial traps.

stories.title: Post Office issues updated savings rulebook
stories.summary: The Department of Posts has released the POSB CBS Manual 2026, the first full revision of its operating rulebook since 2022. The document governs savings operations on the Core Banking Solution platform. While intended for staff, the manual is available for public download on the India Post website.

stories.title: Kerala passes senior citizens protection bill
stories.summary: The Kerala Legislative Assembly passed the Senior Citizens Bill, 2026, to provide state-level protections for older people. The legislation focuses on preventing financial exploitation, cyber fraud, and care-home pressure. It complements existing national laws that allow for the recovery of maintenance payments or the return of gifted property.

stories.title: Defence pensioners abroad gain new life certificate process
stories.summary: Defence pensioners living abroad can now submit manually attested life certificates through authorised Indian bank officials overseas. The Principal Controller of Defence Accounts clarified the process in Circular No. 685, removing the requirement for pensioners to visit embassies or return to India for physical verification. Paperwork now travels instead.

stories.title: Tribunal condones tax appeal delay for Rajasthan woman
stories.summary: The ITAT in Jaipur condoned a 105-day appeal delay for a taxpayer whose father-in-law had been managing her tax affairs before his death. The tribunal also deleted an ad hoc disallowance of business expenses, ruling that officials cannot reject claims without adequate reasons. Deadlines are occasionally flexible for the bereaved.

stories.title: Government transfers 221 crore in latest Sahara refund round
stories.summary: The government has transferred over 10,037 crore to 47.15 lakh depositors through the Sahara refund process. As of November 18, 2026, roughly 1.51 crore people have applied for refunds, with 221.45 crore distributed in the preceding week. Millions of other applicants remain in the queue.

stories.title: ICICI and HDFC Bank offer credit limit increases to select users
stories.summary: ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank are extending credit limit enhancement offers to select customers based on repayment history. Some cardholders report limits doubling without needing to apply for new cards. Eligibility is determined by the banks, and those not selected continue to wait for an offer.

research.title: AI Behavioral Science: A Framework and Agenda
research.summary: Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We discuss the challenges and opportunities present in the rapidly emerging area of ``AI Behavioral Science.'' We frame it via three themes. First, as AI becomes ubiquitous and is increasingly proprietary and opaque, it becomes vital. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: AI, Specialization, and the Organization of Knowledge Work: Evidence from Legal Services
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence makes specialized knowledge cheaper to use, but its effects on professional-service firms depend on how clients reallocate work and how suppliers respond. We develop a framework linking individual self-provision, enterprise make-or-buy decisions, and pricing. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Fooling Yourself: how narratives shape beliefs
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: Narratives often combine diagnostic evidence with truthful but nondiagnostic details. In a two-state experiment with known signal likelihoods, we test whether such details distort belief updating. Although Bayes' rule prescribes no revision, nondiagnostic signals induce revisions. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Human-AI Interactions and Societal Pitfalls
research.summary: Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When working with generative artificial intelligence (AI), users may see productivity gains, but the AI-generated content may not match their preferences exactly. To study this effect, we introduce a Bayesian framework in which heterogeneous users choose. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Recommendation Quality and the Concentration of Consumption: Experimental Evidence from Netflix
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study an experiment with 8.5 million users on Netflix's recommender system to measure how improvements in recommendation technology affect the set of products that get consumed. Improvements increase total consumption and users' reliance on recommendations. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: The Structural Number of Parties: An Electoral-Outcome-Independent Baseline for Comparing Party-System Scale
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: How many parties can a country structurally sustain? Standard measures such as the effective number of parties (ENP) cannot answer this question. They are descriptive and post hoc: they summarize competition only after an election, and. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
